record.paper_title: Open Problems on Graph Coloring for Special Graph Classes
record.original_question: In online graph coloring, vertices are revealed one by one and must be colored irrevocably using only the revealed part of the graph. For each graph G, chi_OL(G) is the minimum, over online coloring algorithms, of the worst-case number of colors used over all vertex orders; a graph class is online chi_OL-bounded if some online coloring algorithm uses at most h(chi_OL(G)) colors for every graph G in the class, for some function h. For every integer k >= 1, is the class of bipartite graphs with no induced path P_k online chi_OL-bounded?

evidence.quote: Open Problem 13 Is the class of Pk-free bipartite graphs on-line χOL-bounded for every k ≥ 1?
We denote the path and cycle on n vertices by Pn and Cn, respectively.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
In the online graph coloring model, the vertices of a graph G are revealed one at a time together with all edges connecting the newly revealed vertex to previously revealed vertices; upon revelation, each vertex must be assigned a color (a positive integer), different from the colors of its already-revealed neighbors, and this assignment is irrevocable. An online coloring algorithm is a (deterministic) rule that produces such a coloring for any input order. For a graph G, let chi_OL(G) denote the minimum, over all online coloring algorithms A, of the maximum number of colors used by A over all possible vertex orderings of G. A class C of graphs is said to be online chi_OL-bounded if there exists a function h: N -> N and an online coloring algorithm A such that for every G in C and every ordering of V(G), the algorithm A uses at most h(chi_OL(G)) colors on G. For a positive integer k, let P_k denote the path on k vertices, and call a graph "P_k-free" if it contains no induced subgraph isomorphic to P_k.

Question: For every integer k >= 1, is the class of P_k-free bipartite graphs online chi_OL-bounded?
artifact.status_search_result: The question is known to hold for small values of k: P_k-free bipartite graphs are online chi_OL-bounded for k up to 9 (results by Micek and others, e.g., the P_8- and P_9-free bipartite cases were established with explicit competitive algorithms). However, the general question "for every k" remains open; no positive result is known for all k, and the broader problem of whether bipartite graphs themselves admit an online competitive algorithm is also still open.

status_evidence.title: An On-line Competitive Algorithm for Coloring Bipartite Graphs Without Long Induced Paths
status_evidence.snippet: On-line competitive algorithm coloring P_9-free bipartite graphs using at most 6(chi*+1)^2 colors.
status_evidence.claim: The class of P_9-free bipartite graphs is online chi_OL-bounded (positive result for k <= 9).

status_evidence.title: An On-line Competitive Algorithm for Coloring P_8-free Bipartite Graphs
status_evidence.snippet: On-line competitive coloring algorithm for P_8-free bipartite graphs.
status_evidence.claim: Positive result is known for k = 8.

status_evidence.title: Open Problems on Graph Coloring for Special Graph Classes
status_evidence.snippet: Only partial positive results for bipartite graphs with certain small forbidden induced subgraphs; the question for all k is listed as open.
status_evidence.claim: The question for all k >= 1 remains open.
